+title: 'validator findings: crates/claude-agent/src/protocol_translator.rs (pre-existing)'
+---
+Pre-existing validator findings surfaced by `review file crates/claude-agent/src/protocol_translator.rs` on 2026-08-08. None of these lines belong to card ^811xj0q (warm prefix reuse telemetry); that card only added `CacheUsage::META_KEY` at lines 49-57. Filed separately so ^811xj0q is not blocked by code it never touched.
+
+## Review Findings (2026-08-08 05:12)
+
+- [ ] `crates/claude-agent/src/protocol_translator.rs:111` — missing documentation for a struct field.
+- [ ] `crates/claude-agent/src/protocol_translator.rs:118` — ProtocolTranslator is a public struct but does not implement Debug. Per validator rule, all public types must implement applicable traits; Debug is essential for testability and debugging. Implement Debug manually (if the inner type doesn't derive it) or ensure PermissionPolicyEngine derives Debug so ProtocolTranslator can derive it: `#[derive(Debug)]`.
+- [ ] `crates/claude-agent/src/protocol_translator.rs:155` — Public function acp_to_stream_json accepts Vec<ContentBlock> when it should accept &[ContentBlock]. Violates rule: 'Accept generics, not concrete types. ... &[T] not &Vec<T>'. Using slice references is more flexible and allows callers to pass arrays, slices, or vecs without allocation. Change parameter to `&[ContentBlock]`. Update line 162 to pass the slice directly: `self.convert_content_blocks_to_items(content)?`.
+- [ ] `crates/claude-agent/src/protocol_translator.rs:171` — Methods `serialize_simple_text_message` (lines 171–183) and `serialize_array_message` (lines 245–257) are 90% identical: both construct a `StreamJsonUserMessage`, serialize it the same way, and produce identical error messages. The only difference is the `content` field: one uses `UserMessageContent::String(text.to_string())`, the other `UserMessageContent::Array(content_items)`. This is one function with an argument waiting to be extracted — the duplication inflates surface area and creates a maintenance burden when the serialization logic needs to change. Extract a shared helper method `fn serialize_user_message(&self, content: UserMessageContent) -> Result<String>` that constructs the message and serializes it. Call it from both methods: `serialize_simple_text_message` becomes `self.serialize_user_message(UserMessageContent::String(text.to_string()))` and `serialize_array_message` becomes `self.serialize_user_message(UserMessageContent::Array(content_items))`.
+- [ ] `crates/claude-agent/src/protocol_translator.rs:461` — `handle_assistant_text` reimplements text extraction and notification building that exists in claude.rs. The 0.90 similarity with `ClaudeClient::extract_text_from_line` indicates nearly identical logic for extracting text from JSON and creating notifications in the same crate. The capability should be reused rather than duplicated. Call or delegate to `ClaudeClient::extract_text_from_line` or similar existing methods instead of reimplementing JSON text extraction and notification creation.
+- [ ] `crates/claude-agent/src/protocol_translator.rs:484` — Function `handle_user_message` has condition-nesting depth of 4, which meets the gate limit. Nested if-let expressions (first `if let` at depth 1, second `if let` at depth 2, for loop, third `if let` at depth 4) reduce readability and make control flow harder to follow. Extract the nested condition checking into a separate helper method or use a match-based approach to flatten the nesting.
+- [ ] `crates/claude-agent/src/protocol_translator.rs:567` — The nested type construction `ToolCallContent::Content(Content::new(ContentBlock::Text(TextContent::new(...))))` appears twice (lines 567–571 in `extract_tool_result_content` and lines 599–603 in `parse_tool_content_item`), differing only in the string variable name (`content_str` vs `text`). This is one function with an argument that should be extracted to avoid maintenance burden and inconsistency. Extract a helper method: `fn create_text_tool_content(&self, text: &str) -> agent_client_protocol::schema::ToolCallContent { agent_client_protocol::schema::ToolCallContent::Content(agent_client_protocol::schema::Content::new(ContentBlock::Text(TextContent::new(text.to_string())))) }`. Then line 567–571 becomes `return Some(vec![self.create_text_tool_content(content_str)]);` and line 599–603 becomes `Some(self.create_text_tool_content(text))`.
+- [ ] `crates/claude-agent/src/protocol_translator.rs:667` — `extract_available_agents` reimplements a method that already exists with the same name in the ClaudeClient (claude.rs:479). The shared evidence shows 0.91 similarity — nearly identical implementations in the same crate. Rather than duplicate, this should either call the existing method or both should delegate to a shared utility. Call the existing `ClaudeClient::extract_available_agents` method instead of reimplementing the agent extraction logic, or extract both into a shared utility function and have both call it.
+- [ ] `crates/claude-agent/src/protocol_translator.rs:762` — `categorize_command` reimplements command categorization logic. Similar pattern-matching on command prefixes exists in tool_registry.rs (McpTool::cli_category, 0.86 similarity), suggesting the categorization scheme may already be centralized and should be reused. Check if McpTool::cli_category or another shared categorization utility can be called instead of reimplementing the prefix-matching logic. If the schemes differ, unify them rather than maintain parallel classification code.
+- [ ] `crates/claude-agent/src/protocol_translator.rs:904` — Function `infer_tool_kind` is a hardcoded if-else-if chain over a known set of string patterns (read, write, delete, move, search, bash, fetch). Each branch differs only in the returned ToolKind constant. This should be expressed as a table of (pattern, kind) mappings rather than parallel code paths that must be manually kept in sync. Replace with a data structure like `static TOOL_PATTERNS: &[(fn(&str) -> bool, ToolKind)] = &[(|t| t.contains("read") || t.contains("Read") || t.ends_with("_read"), ToolKind::Read), ...]`. Use a single loop to iterate and return the first match.
+#tool-validators
